Your retake is graded: 3 items correct, 2 partial and 1 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Correct | The model outputs a tool request and doesn't read the calendar itself. |
| q3 | Wrong | You chose "left to run longer, it will eventually fix the bug". |
| q4 | Partial | Your count of 4 is right, but your reason is wrong. |
| q5 | Correct | The result goes back in as the next input. |
| q6 | Partial | The name is only half of what the model sees. |

- **q3:** The same edit gives the same failing test, so step 41 looks like step 40. A step limit that stops the loop and reports so far is the safeguard.
- **q4:** You wrote that the model "runs" each tool. It only writes a request naming the tool, and the program runs it.
- **q6:** The program also gives the model each tool's description and parameters. The model never sees the tool's code, so the description is its only evidence of what the tool does.

**Work on next:** the belief that an agent left to run longer will eventually succeed. Repeated identical failures add no new information, so every loop needs a stopping condition. Also drop the idea that the model runs tools.

**Next step:** write a short Python loop for the makerspace assistant that stops after 10 steps and returns what it did so far. Then state what an unlimited version would do if the test failed every time.

I also added a learning record for this retake and updated your notes. The first attempt (s1) is still ungraded.

The reviewers couldn't read the answer key, so they couldn't check the misconception ids on q3 and q4. I kept the grader's ids and verdicts, and the review record notes this.
